prayerExcerpt.en-US: Am I not here, I who am your mother?
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Não estou eu aqui, eu que sou tua mãe?

meta.face: A Nahua man of about fifty-seven with a broad, high-cheekboned indigenous face, warm brown skin, straight black hair cut in a thick fringe across the forehead and falling straight to the jaw, CLEAN-SHAVEN (no beard, no moustache), dark gentle eyes lowered in humble wonder. He must not resemble Christ.
meta.basis: The colonial 'true portraits' (Cabrera's Fiel retrato, the Verdadero retrato) show him with long straight black hair, a thin moustache and sparse beard, in a white tilma; he was born in 1474 and was 57 in 1531. Attributes: the tilma with the image, and the roses of Tepeyac.
meta.excerpt: Nican Mopohua v. 119 (Nahuatl, printed by Laso de la Vega, 1649): 'Cuix amo nican nica nimonantzin?'; the Virgin's words to him. Our own translation from the Nahuatl, checked against the transcription at pages.ucsd.edu/~dkjordan/nahuatl/nican/nican5.html
